q-ss-parallel.label: Parallel structure
q-ss-parallel.summary: Items joined by 'and', 'or', 'not ... but' must have the same grammatical form.

q-ss-order.label: Word order in embedded questions
q-ss-order.summary: Inside a sentence, a question word is followed by statement order: where he is staying, not where is he staying.

rules.text: Things joined by and, or, but, or in a list must be in the same form: all nouns, all to-infinitives, or all -ing words.
rules.ok: He likes reading, writing and painting.
rules.bad: He likes reading, to write and painting.

rules.text: In 'not X but Y' (and 'either X or Y', 'both X and Y'), X and Y must match in form. A noun phrase after 'not' needs a noun phrase after 'but'.
rules.ok: It is not the plan but its cost that worries us.
rules.bad: It is not the plan but that it costs too much.

rules.text: A list of abstract nouns cannot end in an -ing form: prudence, propriety and avoidance, not prudence, propriety and avoiding.
rules.ok: Prudence, propriety and avoidance of early disclosure.
rules.bad: Prudence, propriety and avoiding of early disclosure.

rules.text: A question word inside another sentence (know, tell, ask, wonder) is followed by statement order: subject then verb, with no do/does/did and no inversion.
rules.ok: No one knows where he is staying.
rules.bad: No one knows where is he staying.

q-ss-parallel.cue: 'Find the part with the error' or 'choose the best replacement' in a sentence with a list, an 'and', or 'not ... but'.
q-ss-parallel.standard: Mark the joined items. Write each in its bare form. If one is a different form from its partners, that is the error.
q-ss-parallel.fast: Look at the words just before and after 'and' / 'but': they must look alike.
q-ss-parallel.eliminate: Drop options that mix to-forms and -ing forms in the same list.
traps: A list that begins with 'to ...' and then switches to -ing.
'Not X but that ...' mixes a noun phrase and a clause.
Abstract nouns ending a list with -ing.

q-ss-order.cue: A question word (where, what, when, how) in the middle of a sentence after know / tell / wonder / ask.
q-ss-order.standard: Turn the clause into a plain statement: subject, then verb. Choose the option with that order and no extra auxiliary.
q-ss-order.fast: Cross out options that start the clause with an auxiliary (is he, did she).
q-ss-order.eliminate: Remove options with an extra word at the end (staying at) or a wrong tense.
traps: Keeping the question order from the direct question.
Adding 'at' or 'to' where the verb needs none.

pyqs.text:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
What makes the draft legislation especially contentious is not its proposed restructuring of fiscal authority per se, / but that it assumes, without empirical evidence, / a fiscal parity among states whose developmental starting points are / incomparable by any accepted standard.
options: not its proposed restructuring of fiscal authority per se,
but that it assumes, without empirical evidence,
a fiscal parity among states whose developmental starting points are
pyqs.why: 'Not its proposed restructuring' is a noun phrase, so what follows 'but' must be a noun phrase too (for example 'but its assumption, without empirical evidence, of a fiscal parity'). 'But that it assumes' switches to a clause.

a.note: This sets up 'not X' as a noun phrase; it is the model the second part must match, not the error.

c.note: The relative clause 'whose developmental starting points are ...' is correct and continues into the last part.

d.note: 'Incomparable by any accepted standard' correctly completes 'are' from the previous part.

pyqs.text:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:
The doctor advised him [[to stop consuming junk food and doing workouts regularly]].
options: stopping junk food and doing regular workouts
to stop junk food and to workouts regularly
to stop consuming junk food and to work out regularly
to not consume junk food and do workouts
pyqs.why: Both advised actions must be to-infinitives joined by 'and': 'to stop consuming junk food and to work out regularly'. This keeps the same form on both sides.

a.note: 'Stopping ... and doing' is parallel, but it no longer follows 'advised him', which needs 'to ...'.

b.note: 'To workouts' has no verb; 'workouts' is a noun.

d.note: 'To not consume' is a clumsy negative (the usual form is 'not to consume') and the second verb 'do workouts' loses the 'to' and the 'regularly'.

pyqs.trick: Same form each side of 'and': to ... and to ...

pyqs.text:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:
No one knows [[where is he staying]].
pyqs.why: Inside another sentence a question word takes statement order: 'where he is staying'.

a.note: Keeps the question order and also uses the base 'stay' after 'is'.

b.note: Statement order is right, but the extra 'at' at the end is not needed.

d.note: Garbled order; 'is' ends the clause after a past form.

pyqs.trick: Where he is staying: the subject comes before the verb.

pyqs.text:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
The higher the office was / the more pressing became the need / for prudence, propriety, and / avoiding of early disclosure.
options: the more pressing became the need
pyqs.why: 'Prudence, propriety, and ...' is a list of nouns, so the last item must be a noun: 'avoidance of early disclosure', not 'avoiding of'.

a.note: 'The higher the office was' is the correct first part of the 'the ... the ...' pattern.

b.note: 'The more pressing became the need' is the second part of the pattern, inverted for effect and acceptable.

c.note: This begins a list of nouns and is correct; the fault is in the last item.

pyqs.trick: Nouns in a list end with a noun: avoidance.

practice.text:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:
She enjoys [[to swim, cycling and to read]] in her free time.
options: swimming, to cycle and to read
practice.why: 'Enjoys' takes -ing forms, and all three joined items should match: swimming, cycling and reading.

b.note: Still mixes a to-form, an -ing form and a bare verb.

c.note: Mixes a bare verb, a to-form and an -ing form.

d.note: The first item is fixed, but 'to cycle and to read' breaks the match.

practice.text:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:
The manager praised her honesty, / her hard work, and / being punctual / during the review.
practice.why: Honesty and hard work are noun phrases, so the last item should be one too: 'her punctuality'.

a.note: A noun phrase and the first item of the list; correct.

b.note: A noun phrase that matches the first item; correct.

d.note: A prepositional phrase of time; correct.

practice.text:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:
It is not the weather [[but that he was late]] that annoyed us.
options: but to be late of him
practice.why: 'Not the weather' is a noun phrase, so 'but his lateness' matches.

b.note: Garbled; it does not give a noun phrase.

c.note: Garbled word order with no noun phrase.

d.note: This is not grammatical English and gives no noun phrase.

practice.text:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:
I wonder [[what time is it]].
practice.why: After 'wonder', the clause takes statement order: 'what time it is'.

b.note: The words are in an order no English clause uses here.

c.note: Wrong tense for 'wonder' in the present and an extra 'at'.

d.note: The added 'that' is not needed before a question word.

practice.text:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:
Can you tell me [[where does the bus stop]]?
practice.why: Inside 'Can you tell me ...' use statement order and drop 'does': 'where the bus stops'.

b.note: Statement order is right, but the 'does' is left over from the direct question.
